source_refs.note: Book p. 107-111: demand, supply, market equilibrium, consumer and producer surplus, formulae w.r.t. quantity and price, summary table, Examples 60-61, Figures 3.8-3.12

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Aaj hum integration ko bazaar (market) mein le ja rahe hain. Socho aap ek naya mobile lene gaye. Aap dil mein 50,000 tak dene ko tayyar the, lekin dukaan par woh 42,000 ka mil gaya. Aap ne 8,000 "bacha" liye; yeh aap ka faida hai. Economics mein saare khareedaron ke aise faide ka jama consumer surplus kehlata hai. Isi tarah dukaan daar shayad 35,000 mein bhi bech deta, lekin use 42,000 mile; us ka faida producer surplus hai.
Yeh dono faide graph par areas ki shakal mein nazar aate hain, aur area nikalna hum 3.7.1 mein seekh chuke hain. Bas yahi is lesson ka raaz hai.
Economics mein do curves ke darmiyan ka area ek khaas jagah kaam aata hai: consumer surplus aur producer surplus naam ki do miqdaaron (quantities) ka hisaab lagane mein.
Demand Function

Kisi cheez (commodity) ka demand curve batata hai ke har price par khareedar kitni miqdaar khareedne ko tayyar hain. Maan lein \(p\) woh price hai jo khareedar kisi cheez ki miqdaar \(x\) ke liye dene ko tayyar hai. To \(p\) aur \(x\) demand function \(p = D(x)\) se jude hain. Demand function ka graph aam taur par neeche ki taraf jata hai, kyunke qeemat barhe to demand kam hoti hai; yani mehngi cheez log kam khareedte hain. [Figure 3.8]

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: axes O, x (horizontal) and p (vertical). A falling blue curve is labelled p = D(x) and Demand function.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.8: demand function p = D(x) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Supply Function

Maan lein \(p\) woh price hai jis par producer (banane ya bechne wala) kisi cheez ki miqdaar \(x\) bechne ko tayyar hai. To \(p\) aur \(x\) supply function \(p = S(x)\) se jude hain. Supply function ka graph aam taur par upar ki taraf jata hai, kyunke qeemat barhe to producer zyada maal bechna chahta hai. [Figure 3.9]

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: axes O, x (horizontal) and p (vertical). A rising blue curve starting on the p-axis above O is labelled p = S(x) and Supply function.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.9: supply function p = S(x) (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Dono functions mein \(x\) miqdaar (quantity) hai jo horizontal axis par hai, aur \(p\) price hai jo vertical axis par hai.
Demand neeche jati hai: zyada maal bechna ho to qeemat kam karni parti hai, jaise season ke aakhir mein sale lagti hai.
Supply upar jati hai: producer zyada maal tabhi laata hai jab qeemat achhi mile, jaise aam ka rate achha ho to zyada baagh wale mandi mein aate hain.
Market Equilibrium

Jis point par demand aur supply curves ek doosre ko kaat'te hain use market equilibrium (bazaar ka tawazun) kehte hain. Is point par khareedar jitna maal khareedna chahte hain, producer bilkul utna hi bechna chahte hain.
Agar \((x_e, p_e)\) equilibrium point ho to \(x_e\) ko equilibrium quantity aur \(p_e\) ko equilibrium price kehte hain.
Equilibrium point algebra se nikalne ke liye hum demand aur supply ki equations ko ek saath (simultaneous equations ki tarah) solve karte hain.

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: axes O, x and p. A green supply curve rises and a blue demand curve falls; they meet at the dot (x_e, p_e), labelled Equilibrium point. Dashed lines join it to p_e on the p-axis and x_e on the x-axis. The curves are labelled Supply curve and Demand curve.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.10: market equilibrium (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Isay "equilibrium" yani tawazun kyun kehte hain? Tarazu (balance) ka socho: ek palre mein khareedaron ki khwahish aur doosre mein bechne walon ki. Agar qeemat \(p_e\) se zyada ho to maal bach jata hai aur dukaan daar qeemat girate hain; agar kam ho to maal kam par jata hai aur qeemat chadhti hai. Akhir qeemat khud hi us point par aa kar ruk jati hai jahan dono palre barabar hon. Yahi \((x_e, p_e)\) hai.
Amli tareeqa: \(D(x) = S(x)\) rakhein, \(x\) ke liye solve karein (sirf woh root lein jo negative na ho, kyunke miqdaar negative nahi hoti), phir \(p_e = D(x_e)\). Aakhir mein \(S(x_e)\) se check karein ke wohi price aati hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Maan lein ek cheez ki demand \(p = 20 - x\) aur supply \(p = 2 + x\) hai (yeh hamari banayi hui misaal hai). Equilibrium ke liye dono prices barabar rakhte hain:
\[20 - x = 2 + x\]
\[2x = 18, \quad x_e = 9\]
\[p_e = 20 - 9 = 11\]
Check: supply se \(2 + 9 = 11\), wohi price. Yani bazaar mein 9 units 11 rupees fi unit par bikenge. Neeche hum isi misaal se CS aur PS bhi nikalenge.
Consumer Surplus (CS)

Maan lein demand function \(p = D(x)\) hai aur market price \(p_e\) par khareedi gayi miqdaar \(x_e\) hai. Kuch khareedar aise hote hain jo equilibrium price se be-khabar hain aur \(x_e\) miqdaar ke liye \(p_e\) se zyada dene ko bhi tayyar the. Jitna woh dene ko tayyar the aur jitna unhon ne asal mein diya, un ka farq khareedar ka faida hai.
Is tarah consumer surplus ki definition yeh hai:
Consumer Surplus (CS)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein yeh sub-heading "3.4 Consumer Surplus (CS)" chhapi hai. Number 3.4 is unit ke ek pichle section ka hai; yahan yeh sirf 3.7.2 ke andar ek sub-heading hai, is liye isay baghair number ke likha gaya hai.
Consumer surplus woh kul faida hai jo khareedaron ko tab milta hai jab woh cheez equilibrium price par khareedte hain, us zyada price ke bajaye jo woh dene ko tayyar the.
Geometry ki zabaan mein: yeh demand curve ke neeche aur equilibrium point se guzarne wali horizontal line ke upar wala area hai.

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: the supply and demand curves of Figure 3.10 meeting at (x_e, p_e), with the dashed lines to p_e and x_e. The light blue region between the demand curve and the dashed line p = p_e, from the p-axis to the equilibrium point, is labelled Consumer Surplus with an arrow.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.11: consumer surplus (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
Is liye
CS = (Area under demand function from \(x = 0\) to \(x = x_e\)) \(-\) (Area under equilibrium price from \(x = 0\) to \(x = x_e\))
\(= \int_0^{x_e}\) (Demand function) \(dx - \int_0^{x_e}\) (Equilibrium price) \(dx\)

blocks.text_alt: C S equals the integral from 0 to x e of D of x d x minus the integral from 0 to x e of p e d x
C S equals the integral from 0 to x e of D of x minus p e, d x

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Formula ko pattiyon ki zabaan mein parhiye: miqdaar \(x\) par khareedar \(D(x)\) dene ko tayyar tha lekin us ne sirf \(p_e\) diya. Is chhoti si miqdaar \(dx\) par bachat \((D(x) - p_e)\,dx\) hai. 0 se \(x_e\) tak saari bachaton ka jama CS hai.
Doosra integral sirf ek rectangle hai: \(\int_0^{x_e} p_e\,dx = p_e x_e\), yani jo paisa asal mein kharch hua. To CS = (jitna dene ko tayyar the) \(-\) (jitna diya).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Upar wali misaal (\(D(x) = 20 - x\), \(x_e = 9\), \(p_e = 11\)) mein:
\[\text{CS} = \int_0^{9} (20 - x - 11)\,dx\]
\[= \int_0^{9} (9 - x)\,dx\]
\[= \left[9x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^{9} = \dfrac{81}{2}\]
Yani CS = 40.5 rupees. Graph par yeh ek triangle hai jis ka base 9 aur unchai \(20 - 11 = 9\) hai: \(\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 9 = 40.5\). Integral aur triangle dono ek jawab dete hain; seedhi line wale sawalon mein triangle ko check ke liye use kijiye.
Producer Surplus (PS)

Maan lein supply function \(p = S(x)\) hai aur market price \(p_e\) par supply ki gayi miqdaar \(x_e\) hai. Kuch producers \(x_e\) miqdaar ke liye \(p_e\) se kam qeemat bhi qubool kar lete. Jo producers ko asal mein mila aur jitne par woh raazi ho jate, un ka farq producer ka faida hai. Mashhoor economist Alfred Marshall ne is faide ko producer surplus ka naam diya.
Producer Surplus (PS)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein yeh sub-heading "3.5 Producer Surplus (PS)" chhapi hai. Upar wale "3.4" ki tarah yeh number bhi ghalat hai; yeh 3.7.2 ke andar baghair number ki sub-heading hai.
Producer surplus woh kul faida hai jo producers ko tab milta hai jab woh cheez equilibrium price par bechte hain, us kam price ke bajaye jis par woh bechne ko tayyar the.
Geometry ki zabaan mein: yeh supply curve ke upar aur equilibrium point se guzarne wali horizontal line ke neeche wala area hai.

blocks.alt: On a pale yellow panel: the supply and demand curves of Figure 3.10 meeting at (x_e, p_e), with the dashed lines to p_e and x_e. The light blue region between the dashed line p = p_e and the supply curve, from the p-axis to the equilibrium point, is labelled Producer Surplus with an arrow.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.12: producer surplus (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text:
Is liye
PS = (Area under equilibrium price from \(x = 0\) to \(x = x_e\)) \(-\) (Area under supply function from \(x = 0\) to \(x = x_e\))
\(= \int_0^{x_e}\) (Equilibrium price) \(dx - \int_0^{x_e}\) (Supply function) \(dx\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ne yahan "Area above supply function" likha hai. Lekin is ke baad wala integral \(\int_0^{x_e} S(x)\,dx\) supply function ke neeche (under) ka area hai, \(x = 0\) se \(x = x_e\) tak. Sahi: PS = (equilibrium price line ke neeche ka area) \(-\) (supply function ke neeche ka area).

blocks.text_alt: P S equals the integral from 0 to x e of p e d x minus the integral from 0 to x e of S of x d x
P S equals the integral from 0 to x e of p e minus S of x, d x

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Wohi misaal, ab producer ki taraf se (\(S(x) = 2 + x\), \(x_e = 9\), \(p_e = 11\)):
\[\text{PS} = \int_0^{9} (11 - 2 - x)\,dx\]
\[= \left[9x - \dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^{9} = \dfrac{81}{2}\]
PS bhi 40.5 rupees hai. Yahan triangle ka base 9 aur unchai \(11 - 2 = 9\) hai. Producer 2 rupees se upar har unit bechne ko tayyar tha, lekin use har unit ke 11 mile; yahi farq jama ho kar PS banta hai. Total surplus \(40.5 + 40.5 = 81\) rupees.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: CS mein \(D(x) - p_e\) kyun hai aur PS mein \(p_e - S(x)\) kyun? Graph dekhiye: CS wale region mein demand curve upar aur price line neeche hai, jabke PS wale region mein price line upar aur supply curve neeche hai. Hamesha (upar \(-\) neeche), bilkul 3.7.1 ke Note 5 ki tarah.
Consumer Surplus (CS) and Producer Surplus (PS) Formulae
1. With Respect to Quantity (x)
Maan lein:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "\(x_c\) = equilibrium quantity" aur "\(x_e\) = equilibrium price \(= D(x_e) = S(x_e)\)" chhapa hai. Sahi yeh hai: \(x_e\) = equilibrium quantity aur \(p_e\) = equilibrium price \(= D(x_e) = S(x_e)\), jaisa upar likha gaya hai.
Consumer Surplus (CS) = demand curve aur equilibrium price line ke beech ka area, \(x = 0\) se \(x = x_e\) tak: \(\text{CS} = \int_0^{x_e} (D(x) - p_e)\,dx\)
Producer Surplus (PS) = supply curve aur equilibrium price line ke beech ka area, \(x = 0\) se \(x = x_e\) tak: \(\text{PS} = \int_0^{x_e} (p_e - S(x))\,dx\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: PS ke liye kitab ne phir "area between demand curve and equilibrium price line" likha hai. Producer surplus supply curve se banta hai: PS = supply curve aur equilibrium price line ke beech ka area. Saath chhapa formula \(\int_0^{x_e} (p_e - S(x))\,dx\) sahi hai.
Total surplus (TS): \(\text{TS} = \text{CS} + \text{PS}\)

blocks.text_alt: T S equals the integral from 0 to x e of D of x minus S of x, d x

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Total surplus asaan hai: CS aur PS ko jama karein to \(p_e\) wale terms cancel ho jate hain, kyunke ek mein \(-p_e\) aur doosre mein \(+p_e\) hai. Bachta hai demand aur supply curves ke beech ka poora area, yani poore bazaar ka kul faida.
2. With Respect to Price (p)
Maan lein:

items: \(x_d(p) = D^{-1}(p)\) = price \(p\) par demand ki gayi miqdaar
\(X_s(p) = S^{-1}(p)\) = price \(p\) par supply ki gayi miqdaar
\(P_{\max}\) = choke price (is se zyada qeemat par demand zero ho jati hai)
\(P_{\min}\) = minimum price (is se kam qeemat par supply zero hoti hai)

blocks.text: Consumer Surplus (CS) = \(p_e\) aur \(p_{\max}\) ke beech, demand curve \(x_d(p)\) ke neeche ka area:

blocks.text_alt: C S equals the integral from p equals p e to p max of x d of p, d p

blocks.text: Producer Surplus (PS) = \(p_{\min}\) aur \(p_e\) ke beech, supply curve \(x_s(p)\) ke neeche ka area:

blocks.text_alt: P S equals the integral from p equals p min to p e of x s of p, d p

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is tareeqe mein pattiyan leti hui (horizontal) hain, motai \(dp\), aur un ki lambai ek miqdaar hai, \(x_d(p)\) ya \(x_s(p)\), jo \(p\)-axis se curve tak naapi jati hai. Is liye yahan "demand curve ke neeche" ka matlab hai curve aur \(p\)-axis ke darmiyan wala region.
List mein \(X_s(p)\) aur formula mein \(x_s(p)\) ek hi function hain.
Yeh tareeqa tab kaam ka hai jab \(x\) ko \(p\) ki shakal mein likhna aasaan ho, jaise Example 61 mein. "Choke price" ka matlab hai woh qeemat jis par khareedar ka "gala ghut jaye" yani koi bhi khareedne ko tayyar na ho.
3. Summary Table
4. Key Notes

items: Choke price \(p_{\max} = D(0)\) (demand mein \(x = 0\) par price).
Minimum supply price \(p_{\min} = S(0)\) (supply mein \(x = 0\) par price).
\(x\) ke saath integrate karein to limits miqdaarein (quantities) hoti hain aur integrand prices ka farq hota hai.

blocks.title: Example 60
blocks.problem: The supply curve for a good is \(p_s = \sqrt{16 + x}\). The demand curve is linear with vertical intercept 73 and passes through the equilibrium point. If the quantity sold is \(x_e = 33\), find the equation of the demand curve \((p_d)\).
steps:
Diya gaya: supply curve \(p_s = \sqrt{16 + x}\); demand curve ek seedhi line hai jo \(p\)-axis ko 73 par kaat'ti hai; bikne wali miqdaar (quantity) \(x_e = 33\).
Maloom karna: demand curve ki equation \(p_d\).
Tareeqa: equilibrium point dono curves par hota hai. Supply curve se \(p_e\) nikalenge, phir woh seedhi line banayenge jo \((0, 73)\) aur \((x_e, p_e)\) se guzarti hai.

Step 1: Supply curve se equilibrium price
\[p_e = \sqrt{16 + 33} = \sqrt{49} = 7\]
Yani equilibrium point \((x_e, p_e) = (33, 7)\) hai.
Kyun: "quantity sold" hi equilibrium quantity hai, aur us par supply aur demand dono ki price barabar hoti hai. Supply ki equation poori di hui hai, is liye price wahin se mil gayi.

Step 2: Demand line ki shakal
\[p_d = mx + c\]
Vertical intercept \(c = 73\):
\[p_d = mx + 73\]
Kyun: seedhi line ki general form \(p = mx + c\) hai, jahan \(c\) woh value hai jab \(x = 0\) ho, yani \(p\)-axis par intercept. Ab sirf slope \(m\) baqi hai.

Step 3: Point \((33, 7)\) rakhein
\[7 = 33m + 73\]
\[33m = -66\]
\[m = -2\]
Is liye
\[p_d = -2x + 73\]
Kyun: demand line equilibrium point se guzarti hai, is liye yeh point equation ko satisfy karta hai. Slope negative aaya, jo demand curve ke liye bilkul theek hai: qeemat barhe to log kam khareedte hain.
Dhyan dein: 73 ko doosri taraf le jate waqt sign badalta hai: \(7 - 73 = -66\).

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 33\) par \(p_d = -66 + 73 = 7\), aur \(p_s = 7\). Dono curves ek hi price de rahe hain, to \((33, 7)\) waqai equilibrium point hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Example 60 ko ek qadam aage le jate hain (yeh kitab ne nahi poocha, hamari taraf se hai). Ab demand aur supply dono maloom hain, to dono surplus nikal sakte hain:
\[\text{CS} = \int_0^{33} (73 - 2x - 7)\,dx\]
\[= \left[66x - x^2\right]_0^{33} = 1089\]
\[\text{PS} = \int_0^{33} \left(7 - \sqrt{16 + x}\right) dx\]
\[= 231 - \dfrac{2}{3}(343 - 64) = 45\]
Yahan \(\int \sqrt{16 + x}\,dx = \frac{2}{3}(16 + x)^{3/2}\), aur \(49^{3/2} = 343\), \(16^{3/2} = 64\). Dekhiye, khareedaron ka faida producers se kahin zyada hai, kyunke demand line bohat oonchi (73) se shuru hoti hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Example 61 shuru karne se pehle zara graph ka socho. Supply curve \(p = \frac{(x + 10)^2}{25}\) ek parabola ka hissa hai jo \(x = 0\) par \(p = 4\) se shuru hota hai aur \(x = 30\) par \(p = 64\) tak pohanchta hai. Producer surplus woh region hai jo upar se line \(p = 64\) aur neeche se is curve se ghira hai, aur left side par \(p\)-axis hai.
Is region ko do tarah kaat sakte hain. Khari pattiyan (vertical strips) lein to har patti ki lambai \(64 - S(x)\) hai aur \(x\) 0 se 30 tak chalta hai: yeh tareeqa (i) hai. Leti hui pattiyan (horizontal strips) lein to har patti \(p\)-axis se curve tak jati hai, lambai \(x_s(p) = 5\sqrt{p} - 10\), aur \(p\) 4 se 64 tak chalta hai: yeh tareeqa (ii) hai. Region ek hai, is liye jawab bhi ek hi aana chahiye. Exam mein agar sirf ek tareeqa poocha jaye to bhi doosra tareeqa check ke liye bohat kaam aata hai.

blocks.title: Example 61
blocks.problem: If the supply function for a particular commodity is \(25p = (x + 10)^2\) and the market price is Rs. 64, find the producer's surplus by two methods: (i) Integrate with respect to \(x\) (ii) Integrate with respect to \(p\).
steps:
Diya gaya: supply function \(25p = (x + 10)^2\), yani \(p = \frac{(x + 10)^2}{25}\); market price (equilibrium price) \(p_e = 64\) rupees.
Maloom karna: producer surplus do tareeqon se: (i) \(x\) ke saath integrate kar ke, (ii) \(p\) ke saath integrate kar ke.
Tareeqa: (i) \(PS = \int_0^{x_e} (p_e - S(x))\,dx\); (ii) \(PS = \int_{p_{\min}}^{p_e} x_s(p)\,dp\). Dono ke liye pehle \(x_e\) chahiye.

Step 1: Equilibrium quantity
\(p_e = 64\) rakhein:
\[25 \times 64 = (x_e + 10)^2\]
\[(x_e + 10)^2 = 5^2 \times 8^2\]
\[x_e + 10 = 5 \times 8 = 40\]
\[x_e = 30\]
Kyun: \(25 \times 64 = 1600 = 40^2\). Square root lete waqt sirf positive root liya, kyunke miqdaar (quantity) negative nahi ho sakti; \(x_e + 10 = -40\) se \(x_e = -50\) aata, jo bemaani hai.

Step 2: Tareeqa (i), \(x\) ke saath integrate
\[PS = \int_0^{30} \left[64 - \dfrac{(x + 10)^2}{25}\right] dx\]
\[= \left[64x - \dfrac{(x + 10)^3}{25 \times 3}\right]_0^{30}\]
Kyun: kitab ne \(\int_0^{x_e} (p - p(x))\,dx\) likha hai; yahan \(p\) se murad market price \(p_e = 64\) hai aur \(p(x)\) supply price hai. Yani har patti ki height = (jo price mili) \(-\) (jis price par producer bechne ko tayyar tha). \((x + 10)^2\) ka integral \(\frac{(x + 10)^3}{3}\) hai, kyunke andar wale \(x + 10\) ka derivative 1 hai.

Step 3: Limits lagayein
\[= \left(64 \times 30 - \dfrac{40^3}{75}\right) - \left(0 - \dfrac{10^3}{75}\right)\]
\[= 1920 - \dfrac{64000}{75} + \dfrac{1000}{75}\]
\[= 1920 - \dfrac{63000}{75}\]
\[= 1920 - 840 = 1080\]
Kyun: upper limit 30 par \(x + 10 = 40\), aur lower limit 0 par \(x + 10 = 10\).
Dhyan dein: lower limit par doosra term zero nahi hota: \((0 + 10)^3 = 1000\). Isay chhod dena bohat aam ghalti hai.

Step 4: Tareeqa (ii), \(x\) ko \(p\) mein likhein
\[25p = (x + 10)^2\]
\[x + 10 = 5\sqrt{p}\]
\[x = 5\sqrt{p} - 10\]
Kyun: \(p\) ke saath integrate karne ke liye humein quantity ko price ka function chahiye, yani \(x_s(p)\): "is price par kitna maal supply hoga". Dono taraf square root liya: \(\sqrt{25p} = 5\sqrt{p}\).

Step 5: \(p_{\min}\) nikalein (jahan supply shuru hoti hai, \(x = 0\))
\[0 = 5\sqrt{p} - 10\]
\[\sqrt{p} = 2\]
\[p_{\min} = 4\]
Kyun: is price se kam par producer kuch bhi nahi bechega. Key Note wala formula bhi yahi deta hai: \(p_{\min} = S(0) = \frac{100}{25} = 4\).

Step 6: \(p\) ke saath integrate
\[PS = \int_4^{64} (5\sqrt{p} - 10)\,dp\]
\[= \left[\dfrac{5p^{3/2}}{3/2} - 10p\right]_4^{64}\]
\[= \left[\dfrac{10}{3}p^{3/2} - 10p\right]_4^{64}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{p} = p^{1/2}\), aur power rule se \(\int p^{1/2} dp = \frac{p^{3/2}}{3/2} = \frac{2}{3}p^{3/2}\); 5 se multiply karne par \(\frac{10}{3}p^{3/2}\).

Tasdeeq:
Dono tareeqon se PS = Rs. 1080 aaya. Aisa hona hi chahiye tha, kyunke dono ek hi region ka area naap rahe hain: pehle khari pattiyon (vertical strips) se, phir leti hui pattiyon (horizontal strips) se. Jaise ek kamre ka farsh lambai mein tiles laga kar naapein ya chaurai mein, area wohi rehta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 60 ki demand line \(p_d = -2x + 73\) ka choke price kya hai? \(x = 0\) rakhein to \(p_{\max} = D(0) = 73\). Yani 73 rupees ya us se zyada qeemat par koi bhi khareedar nahi milega. Aur supply \(p_s = \sqrt{16 + x}\) ka minimum price \(p_{\min} = S(0) = \sqrt{16} = 4\) hai: 4 rupees se kam par koi producer bechne nahi aayega.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 61 mein agar market price 64 ke bajaye 36 ho to \(x_e\) kitna hoga? \(25 \times 36 = 900 = 30^2\), to \(x_e + 10 = 30\) aur \(x_e = 20\). Ab PS ka integral khud banaiye aur dono tareeqon se check kijiye ke jawab ek aata hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Demand \(p = D(x)\) neeche jati hai; supply \(p = S(x)\) upar jati hai; equilibrium \((x_e, p_e)\) wahan hai jahan \(D(x) = S(x)\).
2. \(\text{CS} = \int_0^{x_e} (D(x) - p_e)\,dx\): demand curve (upar) aur line \(p = p_e\) (neeche) ke beech ka region.
3. \(\text{PS} = \int_0^{x_e} (p_e - S(x))\,dx\): line \(p = p_e\) (upar) aur supply curve (neeche) ke beech ka region.
4. Price ke saath: \(\text{CS} = \int_{p_e}^{p_{\max}} x_d(p)\,dp\), \(\text{PS} = \int_{p_{\min}}^{p_e} x_s(p)\,dp\); \(p_{\max} = D(0)\), \(p_{\min} = S(0)\).
5. Dono tareeqon ka jawab ek hona chahiye; doosre tareeqe ko check ke liye use karein.
6. Seedhi lines ho to CS aur PS triangles hain: \(\frac{1}{2} \times x_e \times\) (unchai).
7. Surplus ka jawab rupees mein likhein, kyunke har patti ka area (price ka farq) \(\times\) (miqdaar) hai, aur price ko miqdaar se zarb dein to paisa hi banta hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Tarteeb ulat dena: CS mein \(D(x) - p_e\), PS mein \(p_e - S(x)\). Surplus negative aaye to samajh lein tarteeb ghalat hai.
2. CS ke liye supply curve ya PS ke liye demand curve use kar lena (kitab ki formula list mein bhi yahi ghalti chhapi hai).
3. \(p\) ke saath integrate karte hue limits 0 se \(x_e\) hi rehne dena; \(dp\) ke saath limits prices honi chahiye.
4. \(x_e\) nikalte waqt negative root le lena; miqdaar kabhi negative nahi hoti, is liye aisa root foran chhor dein.
